subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following is an example of a combination reaction?
explanation: Combination (synthesis) reaction: two or more substances combine to form a single product. CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ is a classic example.

subject: Chemistry
text: The chemical equation 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O is an example of:
explanation: Two hydrogen molecules combine with one oxygen molecule to form water — this is a combination (synthesis) reaction.

subject: Chemistry
text: In the reaction ZnO + C → Zn + CO₂, zinc oxide is:
explanation: ZnO loses oxygen → zinc oxide is reduced. Carbon gains oxygen → carbon is oxidised. This is a redox reaction.

subject: Chemistry
text: Rancidity of food can be prevented by:
options: Keeping in airtight containers with nitrogen
explanation: Rancidity is caused by oxidation of fats. Replacing air (oxygen) with inert nitrogen in airtight packaging prevents oxidation.

subject: Chemistry
text: The reaction between barium chloride and sodium sulphate is:
explanation: BaCl₂ + Na₂SO₄ → BaSO₄↓ + 2NaCl. Both compounds exchange ions → double displacement (precipitation) reaction.

subject: Chemistry
text: The pH of a neutral solution is:
explanation: pH 7 is neutral. pH < 7 is acidic; pH > 7 is basic/alkaline. Pure water at 25°C has pH = 7.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which gas is produced when zinc reacts with dilute sulphuric acid?
explanation: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂↑. Metals above hydrogen in reactivity series displace hydrogen from dilute acids.

subject: Chemistry
text: Baking soda is chemically:
explanation: Baking soda = sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO₃). Washing soda is Na₂CO₃·10H₂O; caustic soda is NaOH.

subject: Chemistry
text: Plaster of Paris is obtained by heating:
explanation: Gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) heated to ~120°C loses 1.5 water molecules → Plaster of Paris (CaSO₄·½H₂O).

subject: Chemistry
text: The common name for sodium hydroxide is:
explanation: NaOH = caustic soda (strongly alkaline, corrosive). Na₂CO₃·10H₂O = washing soda; NaHCO₃ = baking soda.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following is the most reactive metal?
explanation: The reactivity series (K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au). Potassium is the most reactive among the options.

subject: Chemistry
text: The process of extracting metals from their ores using reduction is called:
explanation: Smelting: ore is heated with a reducing agent (coke) at high temperature to extract the metal. Reduction of metal oxide to metal.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which non-metal is a good conductor of electricity?
explanation: Graphite (allotrope of carbon) has delocalized electrons in its layered structure → good conductor of electricity. All other non-metals are insulators.

subject: Chemistry
text: The protective coating of zinc on iron is called:
explanation: Galvanising: coating iron/steel with zinc to prevent rusting. Zinc is more reactive and acts as sacrificial anode.

subject: Chemistry
text: Thermite reaction uses which metal to reduce iron oxide?
explanation: Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe + heat. Aluminium (more reactive) displaces iron. Used for welding railway tracks.

subject: Chemistry
text: The number of covalent bonds in a molecule of methane (CH₄) is:
explanation: Carbon forms 4 covalent bonds. In CH₄: each of the 4 H atoms shares one electron pair with C → 4 C–H bonds.

subject: Chemistry
text: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) reacts with sodium to give:
explanation: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂↑. The –OH group reacts with sodium releasing hydrogen gas (like acid with metal).

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following is a saturated hydrocarbon?
explanation: Saturated hydrocarbons have only C–C single bonds (alkanes). Ethane C₂H₆ is saturated. Ethene (C=C) and ethyne (C≡C) are unsaturated.

subject: Chemistry
text: Saponification is the process of making:
explanation: Saponification: hydrolysis of fat/oil with NaOH → soap (sodium salt of fatty acid) + glycerol.

subject: Chemistry
text: The functional group in carboxylic acids is:
explanation: –COOH is the carboxyl group (functional group of carboxylic acids). –OH = alcohol; –CHO = aldehyde; –CO– = ketone.

subject: Biology
text: Which enzyme in saliva digests starch?
explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) breaks starch → maltose. Pepsin digests proteins in stomach; lipase digests fats; trypsin works in small intestine.

subject: Biology
text: The mode of nutrition in which organisms use sunlight to synthesise food is:
explanation: Autotrophic nutrition: organisms (plants, algae, some bacteria) make their own food using CO₂, H₂O, and light energy via photosynthesis.

subject: Biology
text: In humans, the process of removing waste products from the blood is carried out by the:
explanation: Kidneys filter blood to remove urea, excess salts, and water → urine. Lungs remove CO₂; skin removes some salts via sweat.

subject: Biology
text: Which type of blood vessels carry oxygenated blood from the heart to body organs?
explanation: Arteries carry oxygenated blood away from the heart (exception: pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to lungs). Veins carry blood back to the heart.

subject: Biology
text: The opening and closing of stomata is controlled by:
explanation: Guard cells flank each stoma. When turgid → stoma opens; when flaccid → stoma closes, regulating gas exchange and transpiration.

subject: Biology
text: The basic structural and functional unit of the nervous system is:
explanation: Neuron (nerve cell) is the structural and functional unit. Neurons transmit electrical impulses; nerves are bundles of neuron axons.

subject: Biology
text: Which hormone is produced by the pancreas to regulate blood glucose?
explanation: Insulin (from β-cells of islets of Langerhans in pancreas) lowers blood glucose by promoting glucose uptake into cells and glycogen storage.

subject: Biology
text: The reflex arc involves which of the following in sequence?
options: Receptor → Afferent nerve → Spinal cord → Efferent nerve → Effector
explanation: Reflex arc: Receptor (detects stimulus) → Afferent (sensory) nerve → Spinal cord (nerve centre) → Efferent (motor) nerve → Effector (muscle/gland).

subject: Biology
text: Phototropism in plants is controlled by:
explanation: Auxin (IAA) accumulates on the shaded side of a shoot → cells elongate more → shoot bends toward light (phototropism).

subject: Biology
text: The master gland of the endocrine system is:
explanation: Pituitary gland (hypophysis) is called the master gland as it secretes tropic hormones that regulate other endocrine glands.

subject: Biology
text: Which type of reproduction does not involve fusion of male and female gametes?
explanation: Asexual reproduction: new individuals from a single parent without gamete fusion. Examples: binary fission, budding, fragmentation, spore formation.

subject: Biology
text: Vegetative propagation through leaves is seen in:
explanation: Bryophyllum (Kalanchoe) produces adventitious buds along leaf margins → new plants form. Potato and ginger reproduce from stem modifications.

subject: Biology
text: The part of the flower that develops into fruit after fertilisation is:
explanation: After fertilisation: ovary → fruit; ovule → seed; ovule integuments → seed coat. Petals and stigma wither and fall off.

subject: Biology
text: Double fertilisation is a feature of:
explanation: In angiosperms: one sperm + egg → zygote; second sperm + 2 polar nuclei → triploid endosperm (3n). This is double fertilisation.

subject: Biology
text: In Hydra, reproduction occurs by:
explanation: Hydra reproduces asexually by budding — a small outgrowth (bud) forms on the parent body, grows, and eventually detaches as a new individual.

subject: Biology
text: The physical appearance of an organism due to its genotype is called its:
explanation: Phenotype is the observable characteristic (height, colour, etc.) resulting from gene expression and environment. Genotype is the genetic constitution.

subject: Biology
text: In a monohybrid cross between Tt × Tt, the phenotypic ratio of offspring is:
explanation: Tt × Tt → TT : Tt : tt = 1:2:1 (genotypic ratio). Since T is dominant, TT and Tt both show dominant phenotype → 3 dominant : 1 recessive (3:1 phenotypic ratio).

subject: Biology
text: Sex determination in humans: a child's sex is determined by:
explanation: All eggs carry X; sperm carry either X or Y. If X sperm fertilises egg → XX (female); if Y sperm → XY (male). Father determines the sex.

subject: Biology
text: Acquired characters are NOT inherited because they:
options: Affect the DNA in germ cells
Do not affect DNA in germ cells
explanation: Acquired characters (e.g., muscular body from exercise) do not change the DNA of gametes (germ cells) and therefore cannot be passed to offspring.

subject: Biology
text: Fossils help us understand evolution because they:
options: Provide evidence of organisms that lived in the past
Tell us the age of existing organisms
explanation: Fossils are preserved remains of past organisms, providing direct evidence of extinct species and showing evolutionary relationships between organisms.

subject: Physics
text: The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. This is:
explanation: First law of reflection: angle of incidence = angle of reflection. Both angles are measured from the normal to the reflecting surface.

subject: Physics
text: A concave mirror with focal length 15 cm is used. An object is placed 45 cm from the mirror. The image distance is:

subject: Physics
text: Which mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
explanation: Convex mirrors give an erect, diminished image with a wider field of view → used as rear-view mirrors. Concave mirrors are used as shaving/makeup mirrors.

subject: Physics
text: The refractive index of glass is 1.5. The speed of light in glass is (speed in vacuum = 3×10⁸ m/s):
explanation: n = c/v → v = c/n = 3×10⁸/1.5 = 2×10⁸ m/s. Light slows down when entering a denser medium.

subject: Physics
text: A convex lens has a focal length of 20 cm. Its power is:
explanation: Power P = 1/f (in metres) = 1/0.20 = 5 dioptres (D). Convex (converging) lens has positive power.

chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
subject: Physics
text: The defect of vision in which a person can see nearby objects clearly but not distant objects is:
explanation: Myopia (short-sightedness): image forms in front of retina. Corrected with concave (diverging) lens. Hypermetropia: image behind retina — corrected with convex lens.

chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
subject: Physics
text: The splitting of white light into its constituent colours is called:
explanation: Dispersion: white light splits into VIBGYOR when passing through a prism because different wavelengths refract by different amounts (violet most, red least).

chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
subject: Physics
text: The sky appears blue because of:
explanation: Rayleigh scattering: shorter wavelengths (blue, violet) scatter more in the atmosphere. We see blue because our eyes are more sensitive to blue than violet.

chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
subject: Physics
text: The power of accommodation of the human eye is due to:
explanation: Ciliary muscles adjust the curvature (and hence focal length) of the eye lens to focus objects at different distances — this is called accommodation.

chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
subject: Physics
text: A person uses a concave lens of power –2.5 D. The defect of vision is:
explanation: Concave (diverging) lens has negative power → used to correct myopia (near-sightedness), where the image forms in front of the retina.

subject: Physics
text: Ohm's law states that at constant temperature:
explanation: Ohm's law: V ∝ I, i.e., V = IR where R is constant at constant temperature. More precisely V/I = constant = R.

subject: Physics
text: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω, and 6 Ω are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance is:
explanation: 1/R = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 3/6 + 2/6 + 1/6 = 6/6 = 1. Therefore R = 1 Ω. Parallel resistance is always less than the smallest individual resistance.

subject: Physics
text: The SI unit of electric charge is:
explanation: Coulomb (C) is the SI unit of electric charge. Current (A) = charge (C) / time (s). Named after physicist Charles-Augustin de Coulomb.

subject: Physics
text: The heating element of an electric iron is made of:
explanation: Nichrome (Ni-Cr alloy): high resistivity, high melting point, does not oxidise at high temperatures → ideal for heating elements in electric appliances.

subject: Physics
text: If a bulb of 100 W is used for 10 hours, the electrical energy consumed is:
explanation: Energy = Power × Time = 100 W × 10 h = 1000 Wh = 1 kWh (1 unit of electricity). This is the unit used by electricity meters.

subject: Physics
text: The magnetic field lines of a bar magnet:
options: Begin at N and end at S externally
explanation: Magnetic field lines are always closed loops — outside the magnet from N to S, and inside from S to N. They never intersect each other.

subject: Physics
text: A current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field experiences a force. This is the basis of:
explanation: Electric motor uses the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field to convert electrical energy → mechanical (rotational) energy.

subject: Physics
text: The device used to convert AC to DC is a:
explanation: Rectifier (using diodes) converts AC → DC. Transformers change AC voltage levels; generators produce electricity; inductors store magnetic energy.

subject: Physics
text: According to Fleming's Right Hand Rule, if the thumb points in the direction of motion and the index finger in the direction of the field, the middle finger points in the direction of:
explanation: Fleming's Right Hand Rule (for generators/electromagnetic induction): thumb = motion, index = field, middle finger = induced current direction.

subject: Physics
text: The frequency of AC supply in India is:
explanation: India uses 50 Hz AC supply at 220 V (230 V nominal). USA uses 60 Hz at 110/120 V. Frequency = number of complete cycles per second.

subject: Physics
text: Which of the following is a non-renewable source of energy?
explanation: Coal is a fossil fuel — formed over millions of years and cannot be replenished at human timescales. Solar, wind, and tidal are renewable sources.

subject: Physics
text: The energy released in a nuclear reactor comes from:
explanation: Nuclear reactors use controlled nuclear fission (splitting of heavy nuclei like U-235 or Pu-239) to release enormous amounts of energy (E = mc²).

subject: Physics
text: Biogas is mainly composed of:
explanation: Biogas is ~55–65% methane (CH₄), plus CO₂ and traces of other gases. Produced by anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in biogas plants.

subject: Physics
text: Solar cells convert:
explanation: Solar cells (photovoltaic cells) use the photovoltaic effect to convert light energy (photons) directly to electrical energy (DC electricity).

subject: Physics
text: The minimum temperature required for nuclear fusion is approximately:
explanation: Nuclear fusion requires extremely high temperatures (~10–15 million °C / 10⁷ K) to overcome the electrostatic repulsion between positively charged nuclei.

subject: Biology
text: The flow of energy in a food chain is:
explanation: Energy flows unidirectionally (one-way) from sun → producers → primary consumers → secondary consumers → tertiary consumers. It is not recycled.

subject: Biology
text: Which of the following is a biodegradable pollutant?
explanation: Sewage (organic waste) is decomposed by microorganisms → biodegradable. Plastic, DDT, and mercury are non-biodegradable and persist in the environment.

subject: Biology
text: Ozone (O₃) in the stratosphere protects us from:
explanation: The stratospheric ozone layer absorbs harmful UV-B and UV-C radiation from the sun, protecting living organisms from DNA damage and skin cancer.

subject: Biology
text: The phenomenon of accumulation of non-biodegradable chemicals in organisms at each trophic level is called:
explanation: Biomagnification (biological magnification): concentration of persistent chemicals (DDT, mercury) increases at each successive trophic level in a food chain.

subject: Biology
text: The number of trophic levels in a food chain is generally limited to:
explanation: Only 10% of energy is transferred to the next trophic level (10% law). After 3–4 levels, energy is too little to sustain another consumer level.

subject: Biology
text: The 3 R's of waste management stand for:
explanation: The 3R principle: Reduce (use less), Reuse (use again), Recycle (process into new products). Followed in this priority order to minimise waste.

subject: Biology
text: The Bishnoi community of Rajasthan is known for protecting:
explanation: In 1730, Amrita Devi Bishnoi sacrificed her life along with 363 others protecting Khejri trees from being cut down by royal soldiers — a pioneering conservation movement.

subject: Biology
text: Coliform bacteria in drinking water indicates contamination from:
explanation: Coliform bacteria (e.g., E. coli) originate in the gut of warm-blooded animals. Their presence in water is an indicator of faecal contamination.

subject: Biology
text: Chipko movement was started to protect:
explanation: Chipko movement (1973, Uttarakhand): villagers hugged trees (chipko = embrace/cling) to prevent logging, protecting Himalayan forests from commercial felling.

subject: Biology
text: The 'Khadin' system is a traditional water harvesting structure found in:
explanation: Khadin: an earthen embankment built across the foot of hill slopes in Rajasthan to trap monsoon runoff for cultivation — ancient rainwater harvesting technique.

subject: Chemistry
text: In the modern periodic table, elements are arranged in order of increasing:
explanation: Moseley's modern periodic law: properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers. Elements are arranged by increasing atomic number (Z).

subject: Chemistry
text: The element in period 3 and group 1 is:
explanation: Period 3 starts with Na (Z=11) in group 1. Li is period 2, group 1; K is period 4, group 1; Mg is period 3 but group 2.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which property generally decreases across a period from left to right?
explanation: Across a period: nuclear charge increases, pulling electrons closer → atomic radius decreases. Electronegativity and ionisation energy increase across a period.

subject: Chemistry
text: The valency of an element equals the number of:
options: Electrons in outermost shell capable of bonding
explanation: Valency = electrons in the outermost shell that can be lost, gained, or shared to achieve stability (8 electrons / noble gas configuration).

subject: Chemistry
text: Non-metals are generally located in the periodic table at the:
explanation: Non-metals occupy the top-right portion of the periodic table (with exception of hydrogen at top-left). The staircase/zigzag line separates metals from non-metals.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following is an ester?
explanation: Ethyl ethanoate (CH₃COOC₂H₅) is an ester formed by esterification of acetic acid and ethanol. Esters have the –COO– functional group and characteristic fruity smells.

subject: Chemistry
text: The IUPAC name of CH₃-CH₂-OH is:
explanation: CH₃-CH₂-OH has 2 carbons → ethanol (eth = 2 carbons, -ol suffix for alcohol). IUPAC name: ethanol. Common name: alcohol or ethyl alcohol.

subject: Chemistry
text: Addition reaction is characteristic of:
explanation: Unsaturated compounds (alkenes, alkynes) undergo addition reactions across the double/triple bond. Saturated alkanes undergo substitution reactions.

subject: Biology
text: Stomata open during the day because:
options: Guard cells become turgid due to photosynthesis
explanation: During daytime, guard cells photosynthesize → produce glucose → osmotic pressure increases → water enters → cells become turgid → stomata open for gas exchange.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following reactions is endothermic?
explanation: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ requires heating (heat energy is absorbed from surroundings) → endothermic. Combustion and respiration are exothermic.

subject: Physics
text: What happens to the resistance of a conductor when its length is doubled?
explanation: R = ρL/A. If L doubles (area constant): R doubles. Resistance is directly proportional to length and inversely proportional to cross-sectional area.

subject: Physics
text: Two bulbs of 40 W and 60 W are connected in series. Which bulb glows brighter?
explanation: In series, same current flows. P = I²R. R = V²/P, so 40 W bulb has higher resistance → dissipates more power in series → glows brighter. (Opposite of parallel.)

subject: Physics
text: An AC generator works on the principle of:
explanation: AC generator converts mechanical energy → electrical energy using Faraday's law: a coil rotating in a magnetic field experiences changing flux → induces alternating EMF.

subject: Biology
text: The genotypic ratio from a monohybrid cross Tt × Tt is:
explanation: Tt × Tt → TT : Tt : tt = 1:2:1 (genotypic ratio). TT and Tt show dominant phenotype → phenotypic ratio is 3:1.

subject: Biology
text: In binary fission, a single organism divides into:
explanation: Binary fission: the cell divides into two equal daughter cells (e.g., Amoeba, bacteria). It is the simplest form of asexual reproduction.

subject: Physics
text: Virtual image is formed by a:
options: Concave mirror when object is beyond C
explanation: Concave lens always forms virtual, erect, diminished images. Convex mirror always forms virtual, erect, diminished images. Both are correct.

subject: Physics
text: A ray of light passing through the optical centre of a lens:
options: Bends away from the principal axis
explanation: A ray through the optical centre of a lens passes straight through without any deviation, regardless of the lens type (concave or convex).

subject: Chemistry
text: The acid present in vinegar is:
explanation: Vinegar contains 5–8% acetic acid (ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH). Citric acid is in citrus fruits; tartaric acid in tamarind; oxalic acid in spinach.

subject: Chemistry
text: Metals are generally:
explanation: Metals have free electrons → good conductors of both heat and electricity. They are electropositive, lustrous (shiny), malleable, and ductile.

subject: Biology
text: Greenhouse gases trap heat energy and lead to:
explanation: Greenhouse gases (CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, H₂O vapour) absorb outgoing infrared radiation → trap heat → global warming → climate change.

subject: Biology
text: The neurotransmitter released at the synapse is:
explanation: Acetylcholine (and other neurotransmitters like dopamine, serotonin) are released from synaptic vesicles at the synapse to transmit nerve impulses across the gap.

subject: Physics
text: Which fuel has the highest calorific value?
explanation: Calorific values (kJ/g): wood ~17, coal ~30, petroleum ~45, hydrogen ~150. Hydrogen has the highest energy content per unit mass of all known fuels.

subject: Biology
text: The site of photosynthesis in a plant cell is:
explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll (green pigment) and are the site of photosynthesis. Mitochondria are sites of cellular respiration (energy release).

subject: Chemistry
text: The number of periods in the modern periodic table is:
explanation: The modern periodic table has 7 horizontal rows called periods and 18 vertical columns called groups. Period 6 contains lanthanides; period 7 contains actinides.

subject: Chemistry
text: A substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being consumed is called a:
explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy of a reaction, speeding it up without being consumed or appearing in the final products. MnO₂ catalyses H₂O₂ decomposition.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following is amphoteric?
explanation: Al₂O₃ (aluminium oxide) is amphoteric — reacts with both acids (Al₂O₃ + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂O) and bases (Al₂O₃ + 2NaOH → 2NaAlO₂ + H₂O).

subject: Chemistry
text: The next higher homologue of ethane in the alkane series is:
explanation: Homologous series of alkanes: methane (CH₄), ethane (C₂H₆), propane (C₃H₈), butane (C₄H₁₀)... Each successive member has one more CH₂ unit.

subject: Physics
text: The unit of electric potential difference is:
explanation: Volt (V) is the SI unit of potential difference (voltage). 1 Volt = 1 Joule/Coulomb. Named after Alessandro Volta.

subject: Physics
text: Which rule is used to find the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field?
explanation: Fleming's Left Hand Rule: for motors, when forefinger = field direction and middle finger = current direction, the thumb gives the direction of force (motion).

subject: Biology
text: Darwin's theory of evolution is based on:
options: Natural selection and survival of the fittest
explanation: Darwin: organisms with favourable variations survive ('survival of the fittest') and reproduce more → these traits are passed to offspring → evolution by natural selection.

subject: Chemistry
text: By the law of conservation of mass, if 4.8 g of magnesium burns completely in oxygen to form 8.0 g of magnesium oxide, the mass of oxygen that reacted is:
explanation: Law of conservation of mass: total mass of reactants = total mass of products. Mass of oxygen = mass of MgO − mass of Mg = 8.0 − 4.8 = 3.2 g.

subject: Chemistry
text: When aluminium reacts with oxygen, the balanced equation is 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃. The sum of all the coefficients in this balanced equation is:
explanation: Adding all coefficients: 4 (Al) + 3 (O₂) + 2 (Al₂O₃) = 9.

subject: Chemistry
text: In the thermite reaction Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe + heat, which statement best describes the reaction?
options: It is a double displacement reaction only
It is a decomposition reaction that absorbs heat
It is both a displacement and a redox reaction, and it is exothermic
It is only a displacement reaction and is endothermic
explanation: Aluminium displaces iron from its oxide (displacement), Fe₂O₃ is reduced while Al is oxidised (redox), and large heat is released, melting the iron — so it is an exothermic displacement/redox reaction.

subject: Chemistry
text: The decomposition of silver bromide (2AgBr → 2Ag + Br₂), used in black-and-white photography, is triggered mainly by:
explanation: This is a photolytic (photochemical) decomposition reaction — light energy breaks AgBr into silver and bromine, which is the basis of photographic film development.

subject: Chemistry
text: In the reaction ZnO + C → Zn + CO, carbon acts as the:
explanation: Carbon gains oxygen (C → CO) and is itself oxidised, which means it causes the reduction of ZnO to Zn — so carbon is the reducing agent.

subject: Chemistry
text: A reaction in which two compounds exchange ions to form two new compounds is called a:
explanation: Double displacement reaction: ions are exchanged between two reacting compounds, often forming an insoluble precipitate, e.g. AgNO₃ + NaCl → AgCl↓ + NaNO₃.

subject: Chemistry
text: Rusting of iron is a chemical process that mainly involves:
explanation: Rusting is the oxidation of iron: iron reacts with oxygen and moisture in the air to form hydrated iron(III) oxide (rust), Fe₂O₃·xH₂O.

subject: Chemistry
text: The pH of a solution changes from 3 to 5. By what factor does the H⁺ ion concentration decrease?
explanation: pH = −log[H⁺], and pH is a logarithmic (base-10) scale. An increase in pH by 2 units means [H⁺] decreases by 10² = 100 times.

subject: Chemistry
text: Equal volumes of a strong HCl solution and a NaOH solution exactly neutralise each other. If the same volume of HCl is first diluted 10 times with water and then mixed with the same volume and concentration of the NaOH solution, the resulting mixture will be:
explanation: Diluting the HCl reduces the moles of H⁺ available, while the amount of NaOH stays the same, so NaOH is now in excess after mixing — the resulting solution turns basic.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which pair of reactants, when combined in the correct proportion, produces a salt whose aqueous solution is neutral (pH = 7)?
explanation: A salt of a strong acid and a strong base (like NaCl from HCl + NaOH) is neutral. Salts formed from a weak acid/base combination (e.g. sodium acetate, ammonium chloride) are basic or acidic respectively.

subject: Chemistry
text: Tooth decay begins when the pH inside the mouth falls below approximately:
explanation: Bacteria in the mouth produce acids from sugar residues. When mouth pH drops below 5.5, tooth enamel (calcium phosphate/hydroxyapatite) starts to corrode, causing decay.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which salt is commonly used to remove the permanent hardness of water and is also known as washing soda?
explanation: Washing soda (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O) precipitates the Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions responsible for permanent hardness of water as insoluble carbonates, softening the water.

subject: Chemistry
text: An acid turns blue litmus paper:
explanation: Acids turn blue litmus paper red, while bases turn red litmus paper blue. This is a standard acid-base indicator test.

subject: Chemistry
text: A metal X displaces metal Y from its salt solution but does NOT react with dilute HCl to liberate hydrogen gas. X is most likely:
explanation: Copper lies below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace H₂ from dilute acids, but it can still displace less reactive metals like silver from their salt solutions (Cu + 2AgNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2Ag).

subject: Chemistry
text: An element X forms an oxide X₂O₃ that reacts with both acids and bases. X does not react with cold water but reacts with steam to liberate hydrogen. X is most likely:
explanation: Aluminium forms the amphoteric oxide Al₂O₃ (reacts with both acids and alkalis) and, being moderately reactive, reacts with steam but not cold water — matching both given clues.

subject: Chemistry
text: Ionic compounds generally have high melting and boiling points because:
options: They have covalent bonds that are weak
They exist as small, light molecules
There is a strong electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions in the crystal lattice
explanation: Ionic compounds form a rigid crystal lattice held together by strong electrostatic attraction between cations and anions, requiring a large amount of energy to break — hence high melting/boiling points.

subject: Chemistry
text: In the extraction of aluminium, the ore bauxite is first purified to remove impurities before electrolysis. This purification process is known as the:
explanation: Bauxite (impure Al₂O₃) is purified by the Baeyer's process before it is subjected to electrolytic reduction (Hall-Héroult process) to extract aluminium metal.

subject: Chemistry
text: Non-metals generally form oxides that are:
explanation: Non-metal oxides are generally acidic (e.g. CO₂, SO₂ dissolve in water to form acids) or occasionally neutral (e.g. CO, H₂O), unlike metal oxides which are usually basic.

subject: Chemistry
text: Using the general formula for alkanes, CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, the molecular formula of the alkane with n = 4 is:
explanation: For alkanes, CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. With n = 4: C₄H(2×4+2) = C₄H₁₀, which is butane.

subject: Chemistry
text: How many structural isomers does butane (C₄H₁₀) have?
explanation: Butane (C₄H₁₀) has two structural isomers: straight-chain n-butane and branched isobutane (2-methylpropane), both with the same molecular formula but different structures.

subject: Chemistry
text: When a hydrocarbon burns in air with a yellow, sooty flame producing visible black smoke, this indicates that the hydrocarbon is most likely:
explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons have a higher proportion of carbon and burn with incomplete combustion in air, producing a yellow sooty flame with unburnt carbon particles (soot/smoke).

subject: Chemistry
text: Sodium hydrogen carbonate is added to ethanoic acid (vinegar), and the gas evolved is passed through freshly prepared lime water. What is observed?
options: The lime water turns milky due to CO₂ formed
explanation: CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂↑. The CO₂ evolved reacts with lime water (Ca(OH)₂) to form insoluble CaCO₃, turning it milky — a standard confirmatory test for both the acid and the gas.

subject: Chemistry
text: Hard water containing dissolved Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions forms a scum with ordinary soap because:
options: The ions neutralise the soap's alkalinity
Soap dissolves completely and the scum is just excess soap
Soap reacts with these ions to form insoluble calcium/magnesium salts of fatty acids
explanation: Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions react with the sodium/potassium salts of fatty acids in soap to form insoluble calcium/magnesium stearate (scum), wasting the soap and reducing its cleaning efficiency.

subject: Chemistry
text: The IUPAC name of CH₃–CO–CH₃ is:
explanation: CH₃–CO–CH₃ (acetone) has a ketone (–CO–) functional group with 3 carbons, so its IUPAC name uses the suffix '-one' → propanone.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following has the general molecular formula CₙH₂ₙ?
explanation: Alkenes (containing one C=C double bond) follow the general formula CₙH₂ₙ. Alkanes follow CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ and alkynes follow CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.

subject: Chemistry
text: Carbon has how many valence electrons in its outermost shell?
explanation: Carbon's electronic configuration is 2,4 — it has 4 electrons in its outermost shell, giving it a valency of 4 and allowing it to form 4 covalent bonds.

subject: Chemistry
text: The property of carbon atoms to form long chains by bonding with other carbon atoms is called:
explanation: Catenation is the self-linking property of carbon, allowing it to form long chains, branched chains, and rings — a key reason for the vast diversity of organic compounds.

subject: Biology
text: Oxygenated blood returning from the lungs first enters which chamber of the human heart?
explanation: The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs into the left atrium, which then passes it to the left ventricle for pumping to the rest of the body.

subject: Biology
text: Which sequence correctly represents the pathway of deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the left atrium?
options: Right ventricle → pulmonary vein → lungs → pulmonary artery → left atrium
Right ventricle → vena cava → lungs → pulmonary artery → left atrium
Right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium
Right ventricle → aorta → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium
explanation: Deoxygenated blood leaves the right ventricle via the pulmonary artery to the lungs for oxygenation, and returns as oxygenated blood via the pulmonary vein into the left atrium.

subject: Biology
text: Bile, produced by the liver and stored in the gallbladder, aids fat digestion mainly by:
options: Directly absorbing fat into the bloodstream
Emulsifying large fat globules into smaller droplets, increasing surface area for enzyme action
Chemically breaking fat molecules into fatty acids and glycerol
Neutralising excess acid produced in the small intestine only
explanation: Bile does not contain digestive enzymes; it emulsifies fats into tiny droplets, greatly increasing the surface area available for lipase enzymes to chemically digest the fat efficiently.

subject: Biology
text: During heavy exercise, when the oxygen supply to muscle cells is insufficient, anaerobic respiration in muscles produces:
explanation: When oxygen is limited, muscle cells break down glucose anaerobically to lactic acid (instead of the complete aerobic breakdown to CO₂ and water), causing muscle fatigue and cramps.

subject: Biology
text: Xylem tissue in plants transports water and dissolved minerals mainly in which direction?
options: Both upward and downward, depending on need
Downward, from leaves to roots only
Sideways, from stem to nearby plants
explanation: Unlike phloem (which transports food bidirectionally), xylem transports water and minerals unidirectionally, upward from the roots to the rest of the plant, driven mainly by transpiration pull.

subject: Biology
text: The functional and structural unit of the kidney is called the:
explanation: Each kidney contains millions of nephrons, the basic filtration units responsible for forming urine by filtering blood and reabsorbing useful substances.

subject: Biology
text: Which organ is primarily responsible for pumping blood throughout the human body?
explanation: The heart is a muscular pump that rhythmically contracts to circulate blood through arteries, capillaries, and veins to all parts of the body.

subject: Biology
text: In a knee-jerk reflex, the response occurs almost instantly and only afterward does the person consciously perceive the stimulus. This best demonstrates that:
options: The reflex is controlled by the spinal cord independently, though the brain is informed of the stimulus afterward
Reflexes are always consciously controlled by the brain in real time
The spinal cord and brain act simultaneously with equal speed
Reflex actions do not involve the nervous system at all
explanation: Reflex arcs are processed at the spinal cord level for a rapid, involuntary response, bypassing the need to wait for the brain — the brain only becomes aware of the sensation slightly afterward via a separate pathway.

subject: Biology
text: A person with damage to the cerebellum would most likely show problems with:
options: Balance and coordination of voluntary movements
Involuntary control of heart rate and breathing
explanation: The cerebellum, part of the hindbrain, is responsible for maintaining posture, balance, and precise coordination of voluntary movements. Heart rate/breathing are controlled by the medulla; temperature by the hypothalamus.

subject: Biology
text: Which plant hormone promotes cell division and helps delay the ageing (senescence) of leaves?
explanation: Cytokinins promote cell division (cytokinesis) and are known to delay senescence in leaves by keeping them metabolically active for longer.

subject: Biology
text: Deficiency of iodine in the diet can lead to enlargement of which gland, a condition known as goitre?
explanation: Iodine is essential for synthesising thyroxine in the thyroid gland. Iodine deficiency impairs thyroxine production, causing the thyroid gland to enlarge (goitre) as it tries to compensate.

subject: Biology
text: The tiny gap between two neurons across which a nerve impulse passes is called a:
explanation: A synapse is the junction between two neurons. Nerve impulses cross this gap chemically, via neurotransmitters released from synaptic vesicles.

subject: Biology
text: A couple wishes to prevent pregnancy using a method that also reduces the risk of transmitting sexually transmitted infections (STIs). The most appropriate choice among the following is:
explanation: Condoms act as a physical barrier that prevents both sperm from reaching the egg and the exchange of body fluids, making them the only listed method that also helps prevent STIs.

subject: Biology
text: In flowering plants, offspring produced through self-pollination followed by fertilisation are, on average, genetically:
options: Less variable and more similar to the parent plant than those from cross-pollination
Completely unrelated to the parent plant
Identical clones of the parent, exactly like asexual reproduction
More variable than those from cross-pollination
explanation: Self-pollination combines gametes from the same plant, so it produces less genetic mixing and offspring more similar to the parent, whereas cross-pollination combines genetic material from two different plants, producing greater variation.

subject: Biology
text: Formation of new individuals from spores, seen in bread mould (Rhizopus), is an example of which mode of reproduction?
explanation: Rhizopus produces spores in sporangia; under favourable conditions each spore germinates into a new individual — a form of asexual reproduction called spore formation.

subject: Biology
text: Which hormone in the human male reproductive system is mainly responsible for the development of secondary sexual characteristics during puberty?
explanation: Testosterone, secreted by the testes, regulates sperm production and triggers secondary sexual characteristics in males such as facial hair growth and voice deepening.

subject: Biology
text: The male gamete produced in the human reproductive system is called the:
explanation: Sperm are the male gametes produced in the testes. They fuse with the female gamete (ovum) during fertilisation to form a zygote.

subject: Biology
text: In Mendel's dihybrid cross for seed shape and colour (RrYy × RrYy), the phenotypic ratio of offspring (round-yellow : round-green : wrinkled-yellow : wrinkled-green) is:
explanation: A dihybrid cross between two heterozygous parents (RrYy × RrYy) produces the classic 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio, showing independent assortment of the two traits.

subject: Biology
text: Human ABO blood groups are controlled by a single gene with three alleles (Iᴬ, Iᴮ, i), where Iᴬ and Iᴮ are both dominant over i but codominant with each other. This inheritance pattern, involving three alleles for one gene, is an example of:
explanation: When a single gene has more than two allelic forms present in a population (here Iᴬ, Iᴮ, i), it is called multiple allelism. Blood group AB additionally shows codominance between Iᴬ and Iᴮ.

subject: Biology
text: The forelimbs of a human, a bat, and a whale have very different functions (grasping, flying, swimming) but share a similar underlying bone structure inherited from a common ancestor. Such organs are called:
explanation: Homologous organs have the same basic structure and evolutionary origin but may perform different functions, providing strong evidence of common ancestry (divergent evolution). Analogous organs, in contrast, have different origins but similar functions.

subject: Biology
text: The wings of a bird and the wings of a butterfly perform the same function (flight) but have completely different structures and evolutionary origins. Such organs are called:
explanation: Analogous organs perform similar functions but differ in structure and origin, arising from convergent evolution rather than shared ancestry — unlike homologous organs.

subject: Biology
text: The scientific study of fossils to trace the evolutionary history of organisms is called:
explanation: Palaeontology is the branch of science dealing with the study of fossils, which provide direct evidence of organisms that existed in the past and their evolutionary relationships.

subject: Biology
text: A sudden, heritable change in the DNA sequence of an organism is called a:
explanation: A mutation is a change in the DNA sequence, which can arise spontaneously or due to external factors, and is one of the important sources of heritable variation for evolution.

subject: Biology
text: Variations that improve an organism's chances of survival and reproduction in its environment are said to be:
explanation: Advantageous variations increase an organism's fitness, giving it a better chance of surviving and passing the trait to offspring — the basis of natural selection.

subject: Physics
text: An object is placed 10 cm from a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. The nature of the image formed is:
explanation: Using 1/v − 1/u = 1/f with u = −10 cm, f = +15 cm: 1/v = 1/15 − 1/10 = −1/30, so v = −30 cm. Since the object lies within the focal length, the lens forms a virtual, erect, magnified image on the same side as the object.

subject: Physics
text: A concave mirror forms a real image 3 times the size of an object placed 20 cm from the mirror. The focal length of the mirror is:
explanation: For a real, magnified image, magnitude of magnification m = v/u = 3, so v = 3 × 20 = 60 cm (taking u = −20 cm, v = −60 cm). Using 1/v + 1/u = 1/f: 1/f = −1/60 − 1/20 = −4/60 = −1/15, giving f = −15 cm, i.e. 15 cm concave mirror.

subject: Physics
text: The refractive index of water is 4/3 and that of glass is 3/2 (both with respect to air). The refractive index of glass with respect to water is:
explanation: Refractive index of glass w.r.t. water = (refractive index of glass w.r.t. air) / (refractive index of water w.r.t. air) = (3/2) / (4/3) = 9/8.

subject: Physics
text: An object 4 cm high is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. The height of the image formed is:
explanation: Using 1/v + 1/u = 1/f with u = −30 cm, f = −10 cm: 1/v = −1/10 + 1/30 = −1/15, so v = −15 cm. Magnification m = −v/u = −(−15)/(−30) = −0.5. Image height = m × object height = −0.5 × 4 = −2 cm (real, inverted, 2 cm high).

subject: Physics
text: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror making an angle of 30° with the mirror's surface. The angle of reflection, measured from the normal, is:
explanation: Angles of incidence and reflection are measured from the normal, not the surface. If the ray makes 30° with the surface, it makes 90° − 30° = 60° with the normal, so the angle of reflection is also 60°.

subject: Physics
text: For a concave mirror, at which object position is a real, inverted image of the same size as the object formed?
explanation: When an object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror, the image formed is real, inverted, and of the same size, also located at the centre of curvature.

subject: Physics
text: The image formed by a plane mirror is always:
options: Virtual, erect, and of the same size as the object
explanation: A plane mirror always forms a virtual, erect image that is laterally inverted and exactly the same size as the object, located as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
subject: Physics
text: A person suffering from hypermetropia has his near point at 1 m instead of the normal 25 cm. To read a book held at 25 cm, the power of the corrective lens required is approximately:
explanation: Using 1/f = 1/v − 1/u with the lens forming a virtual image of the near object at the person's actual near point (u = −25 cm, v = −100 cm): 1/f = −1/100 − (−1/25) = 0.03 per cm, f ≈ 33.3 cm = 1/3 m, so P = 1/f ≈ +3 D.

chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
subject: Physics
text: Myopia (short-sightedness) is corrected using a lens with:
explanation: In myopia, the image forms in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens, which has negative power, diverges the incoming rays slightly before they enter the eye, shifting the image back onto the retina.

chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
subject: Physics
text: The twinkling of stars observed from Earth is mainly caused by:
options: Atmospheric refraction through continuously changing air layers of varying density
Dispersion of starlight by the atmosphere
Scattering of starlight by dust particles
Reflection of starlight from the Moon
explanation: Starlight passes through Earth's atmosphere, which has continuously varying air density and refractive index due to temperature changes. This causes the apparent position and brightness of stars to fluctuate rapidly, producing a twinkling effect.

chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
subject: Physics
text: The scattering of light by colloidal-sized particles suspended in a medium (making a beam of light visible), such as seen when a beam of sunlight passes through dust in a room, is called:
explanation: The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by particles of colloidal size suspended in a medium (like dust in air or fine particles in a liquid), which makes the path of the light beam visible.

subject: Physics
text: A wire of resistance 5 Ω carries a current of 2 A for 10 minutes. The heat produced in the wire is:
explanation: Heat produced H = I²Rt = (2)² × 5 × (10 × 60) = 4 × 5 × 600 = 12,000 J, using Joule's law of heating.

subject: Physics
text: Two resistors of 4 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in series to a 12 V battery. The current flowing through the circuit is:
explanation: In series, total resistance R = 4 + 6 = 10 Ω. By Ohm's law, I = V/R = 12/10 = 1.2 A.

subject: Physics
text: A wire of resistance R is cut into 3 equal parts, and all three parts are then connected in parallel. The new equivalent resistance, in terms of R, is:
explanation: Each piece has resistance R/3. For 3 equal resistors of R/3 in parallel: 1/R_eq = 3 ÷ (R/3) = 9/R, so R_eq = R/9.

subject: Physics
text: A 60 W bulb and a 100 W bulb, both rated for 220 V, are connected in parallel across a 220 V supply (unlike being connected in series). In this parallel arrangement:
options: The 60 W bulb draws more current and glows brighter
Neither bulb glows since they have different power ratings
Both bulbs draw equal current and glow equally bright
The 100 W bulb draws more current and glows brighter
explanation: In parallel, both bulbs get the full rated voltage (220 V), so current I = P/V is higher for the higher-wattage (100 W) bulb, and it dissipates more power, glowing brighter — the opposite of what happens when such bulbs are connected in series.

subject: Physics
text: An electric heater draws a current of 5 A from a 220 V supply. Its power rating is:
explanation: Electrical power P = V × I = 220 × 5 = 1100 W = 1.1 kW.

subject: Physics
text: Electrical power dissipated in a resistor can also be expressed, using Ohm's law, as:
explanation: Since P = VI and V = IR (Ohm's law), substituting gives P = I²R. Equivalently, substituting I = V/R gives P = V²/R.

subject: Physics
text: To obtain the minimum possible equivalent resistance from two given resistors, they should be connected in:
options: Neither; a rheostat must be used
Either way — it makes no difference
explanation: For resistors in parallel, the equivalent resistance is always less than the smallest individual resistance, whereas in series the equivalent resistance is the sum (always higher). So parallel gives minimum resistance.

subject: Physics
text: The commercial unit of electrical energy, as billed by electricity providers, is the:
explanation: 1 kWh (also called 1 'unit' of electricity) = energy consumed by a 1000 W appliance running for 1 hour = 3.6 × 10⁶ J. This is the standard billing unit.

subject: Physics
text: A current-carrying straight conductor placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field experiences a force F = BIL. If the current through the conductor is doubled and the magnetic field strength is simultaneously halved, the force on the conductor will:
explanation: F = BIL. Doubling I (×2) and halving B (×0.5) gives a net factor of 2 × 0.5 = 1, so the force remains unchanged.

subject: Physics
text: A bar magnet's north pole is pushed into a coil connected to a galvanometer. According to Lenz's law, the induced current in the coil flows in a direction such that it:
options: Depends only on the material of the coil, not its direction
Aids the motion of the magnet by attracting it inward faster
Opposes the motion of the magnet (the near face of the coil behaves like a north pole, repelling the magnet)
Has no relationship to the magnet's motion
explanation: Lenz's law states that the induced current always opposes the change causing it (conservation of energy). As the magnet's N-pole approaches, the coil's near face becomes an induced N-pole to repel it, opposing the magnet's motion.

subject: Physics
text: Which of the following devices works on the principle of electromagnetic induction?
explanation: An AC generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy using Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction — a coil rotating in a magnetic field experiences changing flux, inducing an alternating EMF.

subject: Physics
text: The magnetic field produced by a current-carrying circular loop is strongest at the:
options: It is the same everywhere along the loop's axis
Edge of the loop, farthest from the wire
Outside the loop, far from the wire
explanation: The concentric magnetic field lines around each segment of the circular loop add up constructively at the centre, making the magnetic field strongest there.

subject: Physics
text: A current-carrying solenoid produces a magnetic field pattern similar to that of a bar magnet mainly because of:
options: The current flowing through its tightly wound turns of wire
The metal used to make the wire
The colour of the insulation on the wire
Its length being much greater than its diameter
explanation: A solenoid is a coil of many circular turns of wire. When current flows through it, the magnetic fields of each turn add up, producing a strong, uniform field pattern similar to that of a bar magnet, with distinct N and S poles.

subject: Physics
text: An electromagnet is typically made by winding an insulated wire coil around a core of:
explanation: Soft iron is used as the core because it gets magnetised strongly when current flows through the coil but loses its magnetism almost completely once the current is switched off, making it ideal for temporary electromagnets.

subject: Physics
text: In a box-type solar cooker, the glass cover placed over the blackened interior mainly helps by:
options: Reducing the total intensity of sunlight reaching the interior
Reflecting all incoming sunlight away from the cooker
Trapping infrared heat re-radiated by the blackened surfaces, reducing heat loss (a greenhouse-like effect)
Filtering out and blocking all visible light
explanation: Sunlight passes through the glass and is absorbed by the black interior, which re-radiates it as infrared (heat) radiation. The glass cover traps much of this infrared radiation inside (similar to the greenhouse effect), raising and maintaining the internal temperature.

subject: Physics
text: Despite having a high calorific value and producing only water on combustion, large-scale use of hydrogen as a fuel is currently limited mainly because:
options: Safe, efficient storage and transportation of hydrogen gas are difficult and costly
Hydrogen has a very low calorific value
Burning hydrogen produces large amounts of carbon dioxide
Hydrogen does not burn easily in air
explanation: Hydrogen is highly inflammable and has very low density, making its storage, compression/liquefaction, and transportation technically challenging and expensive — this is the main practical barrier to its widespread use as a fuel.

subject: Physics
text: Which of the following is considered the ultimate source of energy for wind, hydro, biomass, and fossil fuel energy (though not for nuclear, tidal, or geothermal energy)?
explanation: Solar energy drives the water cycle (hydro energy), causes uneven heating that creates wind, and is captured by plants via photosynthesis (biomass and, ultimately, fossil fuels), making the Sun the ultimate source for most of these.

subject: Physics
text: A hydroelectric power plant primarily converts which form of energy into electrical energy?
options: The potential energy of water stored at a height into electrical energy
The nuclear energy of water molecules into electrical energy
The chemical energy of water into electrical energy
Solar energy directly into electrical energy
explanation: Water stored at height in a dam has potential energy. As it falls, this converts to kinetic energy, which turns turbines connected to generators, producing electrical energy.

subject: Physics
text: Wind energy, used to generate electricity via windmills, is ultimately derived from:
options: Geothermal energy from the Earth's core
Solar energy (uneven heating of Earth's surface causing air movement)
Nuclear energy stored in the atmosphere
explanation: The Sun heats different parts of the Earth's surface unequally, causing pressure differences in the atmosphere that drive air movement (wind) — so wind energy ultimately originates from solar energy.

subject: Biology
text: In a food chain Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake → Eagle, if grass fixes 10,000 J of energy, approximately how much energy is available to the eagle, applying the 10% law across all four transfers?
explanation: By the 10% law, only about 10% of energy is transferred at each trophic level. After 4 transfers: 10,000 × (0.1)⁴ = 10,000 × 0.0001 = 1 J available to the eagle.

subject: Biology
text: Non-biodegradable pesticides like DDT show increasing concentration at each higher trophic level of a food chain (biomagnification) mainly because:
options: Predators intentionally seek out contaminated prey
Higher trophic level organisms are exposed to more sunlight, which increases the chemical's toxicity
The chemicals become less stable and more concentrated over time on their own
Organisms cannot metabolise or excrete these chemicals efficiently, so they accumulate in body tissue and get further concentrated as predators eat many contaminated prey
explanation: Since these chemicals are not broken down or excreted, they accumulate in an organism's tissues. As each predator consumes many contaminated prey, the concentration increases at each successive trophic level — this is biomagnification.

subject: Biology
text: Which of the following organisms acts as a decomposer in an ecosystem, breaking down dead organic matter?
explanation: Decomposers like fungi and bacteria break down complex organic matter in dead plants and animals into simpler inorganic substances, which are then recycled back into the ecosystem (e.g. into the soil).

subject: Biology
text: The protective ozone layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation, is located in which layer of the Earth's atmosphere?
explanation: The ozone layer is concentrated in the stratosphere, roughly 15–35 km above Earth's surface, where it absorbs most of the sun's harmful UV-B and UV-C radiation.

subject: Biology
text: Green plants and other organisms that can produce their own food are collectively called:
explanation: Producers (autotrophs), mainly green plants and algae, synthesise their own food using sunlight, CO₂, and water via photosynthesis, forming the base of every food chain.

subject: Biology
text: Sustainable management of natural resources primarily aims to balance which two considerations?
options: Completely halting the use of all natural resources immediately
Using resources only in urban areas to protect rural ecosystems
Maximising short-term industrial profit regardless of environmental cost
Meeting present development needs while conserving resources so future generations can also meet their needs
explanation: Sustainable development means utilising natural resources to meet current human needs for development, while ensuring resources are conserved and not exhausted, so that future generations can also meet their own needs.

subject: Biology
text: Rainwater harvesting structures like check dams and percolation pits mainly help by:
options: Directly purifying river water for drinking
Preventing all rainfall from reaching the ground
Generating hydroelectric power on a large scale
Recharging groundwater levels by allowing collected rainwater to seep into the soil
explanation: Rainwater harvesting structures collect and direct rainwater into the ground rather than letting it run off, allowing it to percolate and recharge the groundwater table, which is especially valuable in water-scarce regions.

subject: Biology
text: Switching off unnecessary lights and appliances to lower overall electricity consumption is an example of which of the '3 R's' of resource conservation?
options: None of these — it is unrelated to the 3 R's
explanation: 'Reduce' means minimising the consumption of a resource in the first place. Cutting down unnecessary electricity use lowers demand on natural resources (like coal for power generation) at the source, rather than reusing or recycling something already used.

subject: Biology
text: Which of the following is a renewable natural resource if it is managed and used sustainably?
explanation: Forests can regenerate if harvested sustainably (replanting, controlled felling), making them renewable with proper management, unlike fossil fuels (coal, petroleum, natural gas) which take millions of years to form and are non-renewable on a human timescale.

subject: Chemistry
text: An element X has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 7. In the modern periodic table, X belongs to:
explanation: The number of shells (3) gives the period, so X is in Period 3. Since it has 7 electrons in its outermost shell, it belongs to Group 17 (halogens) using modern group numbering — this element is chlorine.

subject: Chemistry
text: Element A has atomic number 12 (Mg) and element B has atomic number 17 (Cl), both in Period 3. Which statement correctly compares their atomic radius and electronegativity?
options: A has a smaller atomic radius and higher electronegativity than B
A has a smaller atomic radius but lower electronegativity than B
B has a smaller atomic radius and higher electronegativity than A
Both have identical atomic radius and electronegativity since they are in the same period
explanation: Across a period, as atomic number increases, nuclear charge increases and atomic radius decreases while electronegativity increases. Since Cl (17) is further right than Mg (12) in the same period, Cl has a smaller atomic radius and higher electronegativity.

subject: Chemistry
text: Elements placed in the same group of the modern periodic table show similar chemical properties mainly because they have the same number of:
options: Valence electrons (electrons in the outermost shell)
explanation: Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons, which determines their chemical bonding behaviour and reactivity, giving them similar chemical properties despite having different total electron counts.

subject: Chemistry
text: Considering the trend of atomic radius across Period 3, which of the following correctly orders sodium (Na), magnesium (Mg), and aluminium (Al) by increasing atomic radius?
explanation: Atomic radius decreases across a period from left to right as nuclear charge increases and pulls electrons closer. Since the order across Period 3 is Na, Mg, Al (left to right), radius decreases in that order, so increasing radius is Al < Mg < Na.

subject: Chemistry
text: The Modern Periodic Law, stating that properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic number, was given by:
explanation: Henry Moseley established in 1913 that atomic number (not atomic mass) is the fundamental property governing periodicity, leading to the Modern Periodic Law used in today's periodic table.

subject: Biology
text: Which structure in a leaf is mainly responsible for gaseous exchange? (2026 Board)
explanation: Stomata are pores on the leaf surface that open and close to allow gas exchange (O2, CO2, water vapour).
whyWrong: The cuticle is a waxy waterproof layer that prevents, rather than allows, gas/water exchange.
Phloem transports food (organic nutrients), not gases.
Xylem transports water, not gases.

subject: Biology
text: A diagram shows a single-celled organism splitting through several stages into two daughter cells. Identify the type of reproduction shown. (2026 Board)
explanation: A single cell's nucleus and cytoplasm divide to form two independent daughter cells — this is binary fission, as seen in Amoeba.
whyWrong: Spore formation involves specialised reproductive spores, not direct cell splitting.
Fragmentation is breaking into multiple pieces, not a single cell splitting into two.
Budding involves a small outgrowth developing into a new individual, not splitting into two.

subject: Biology
text: Identify the correct statement for spirogyra, leishmania and hydra: (2026 Board)
explanation: Despite differing in cellularity (Spirogyra and Hydra are multicellular, Leishmania is unicellular), all three can reproduce asexually — by fragmentation, binary fission and budding respectively.
whyWrong: They don't all reproduce sexually — fragmentation, binary fission and budding described here are all asexual.
Hydra and Spirogyra are multicellular, not unicellular.
Leishmania is unicellular, not multicellular.

subject: Biology
text: Human brain has various parts or regions that help in different actions, responses and coordination. Identify the part responsible for precision of voluntary actions: (2026 Board)
explanation: The cerebellum is responsible for maintaining posture, balance, and the precision of voluntary movements.
whyWrong: The pons relays signals between brain regions but isn't the seat of movement precision.
The medulla controls involuntary actions like heart rate and breathing, not precision of voluntary movement.
The cerebrum handles voluntary actions' initiation and thinking, not their fine precision/coordination.

subject: Biology
text: Pancreas secretes pancreatic juice which contains certain enzymes that help in digestion of food. Choose the correct option: (2026 Board)
options: Trypsin digests proteins and lipase digests carbohydrates
Trypsin and lipase both digest fats
Trypsin digests emulsified fats and lipase digests proteins
Trypsin digests proteins and lipase digests emulsified fats
explanation: Trypsin is a protease that digests proteins, while lipase acts on emulsified fats, breaking them into fatty acids and glycerol.

subject: Chemistry
text: The emission of brown fumes when lead nitrate crystals are heated in a test tube is due to (2023 Board)
options: thermal decomposition of lead nitrate which produces brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide.
oxidation of lead nitrate forming lead oxide and nitrogen dioxide.
oxidation of lead nitrate forming lead oxide and oxygen.
thermal decomposition of lead nitrate which produces brown fumes of lead oxide.
explanation: Heating lead nitrate is a thermal decomposition: 2Pb(NO3)2 → 2PbO + 4NO2 + O2; the brown fumes are nitrogen dioxide gas.
whyWrong: This is a decomposition reaction (breakdown of one compound on heating), not oxidation by an external agent.

Lead oxide is a solid residue left behind, not the brown fume — the brown fume is nitrogen dioxide gas.

explanation: The balanced equation is MnO2 + 4HCl → MnCl2 + 2H2O + Cl2, so x=4, y=2, z=1.
whyWrong: This does not balance the equation correctly.
This does not balance the Cl, H and O atoms correctly.
This does not balance the equation correctly.

subject: Chemistry
text: The table below has information regarding pH and the nature (acidic/basic) of four different solutions. Which one of the options in the table is correct? explanation: Milk of magnesia (Mg(OH)2) is basic with pH around 10, and turns universal pH paper blue — every detail in this row is correct and consistent.
whyWrong: Lemon juice is acidic (not basic) at pH 3.
Gastric juice is strongly acidic, with a real pH much lower than 6 (around 1.5–3.5).

text: A metal 'X' is used in thermite process. When X is burnt in air it gives an amphoteric oxide 'Y'. 'X' and 'Y' are respectively: (2023 Board)

text: Select washing soda from the following: (2023 Board)
explanation: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na2CO3·10H2O.

subject: Chemistry
text: Consider the structures of three cyclic carbon compounds: A is a six-membered ring with only single bonds (each carbon bearing 2 H atoms, like cyclohexane); B and C are both six-membered rings drawn with alternating double bonds and one H atom per carbon (like two Kekulé structures of benzene). Select the correct option: (2023 Board)
options: A and C are isomers of hexane and B is benzene.
A is an isomer of hexane, B is benzene and C is an isomer of hexene.
A is a saturated cyclic hydrocarbon and B and C are unsaturated cyclic hydrocarbons.
A is cyclohexane and B and C are the isomers of benzene.
explanation: A (all single bonds) is a saturated cyclic hydrocarbon (cyclohexane); B and C (both with alternating double bonds, formula C6H6) are unsaturated cyclic hydrocarbons.
whyWrong: C is unsaturated (has double bonds), so it cannot be an isomer of hexane, a saturated alkane.
C has formula C6H6 (matching benzene), not C6H12 (hexene) — it is not an isomer of hexene.
B and C are two ways of drawing the same molecule (benzene), rather than being distinct isomers of it.

subject: Biology
text: An organism which breaks down the food material outside the body and then absorbs it is (2023 Board)
explanation: Rhizopus (bread mould, a fungus) is a saprotroph — it secretes digestive enzymes onto the food, breaking it down externally, then absorbs the digested nutrients.
whyWrong: Rhizobium is a nitrogen-fixing symbiotic bacterium, not an organism that digests food externally.
Tapeworm is an internal parasite that absorbs already-digested food from its host's intestine.
Cuscuta is a total stem parasite that absorbs ready-made nutrients directly from its host, not by digesting food outside its body.

subject: Biology
text: Consider the following statements about small intestine and select the one which is NOT correct: (2023 Board)
options: The small intestine receives secretions from liver and pancreas.
The length of the small intestine in animals differs as it depends on the type of food they eat.
The villi of the small intestine absorb water from the unabsorbed food before it gets removed from the body via the anus.
The small intestine is the site of complete digestion of food.
explanation: Water from undigested food residue is mainly absorbed in the large intestine, not by the villi of the small intestine — so this statement is not correct.
whyWrong: This statement is correct: the small intestine receives bile from the liver and pancreatic juice from the pancreas.
This statement is correct: intestine length does vary with diet type across animals.
This statement is correct: the small intestine is where digestion is completed.

subject: Biology
text: The statement that correctly describes the characteristic(s) of a gene is: (2023 Board)
options: Each chromosome has only one gene located all along its length.
In individuals of a given species, a specific gene is located on a particular chromosome.
A gene is not the information source for making proteins in the cell.
All the inherited traits in human beings are not controlled by genes.
explanation: Each specific gene occupies a fixed location on a particular chromosome, consistently across individuals of a species.
whyWrong: This is false — each chromosome carries many genes along its length, not just one.
This is false — a gene is exactly the information source used to make a specific protein.

subject: Biology
text: Select from the following the correct statement about tropic movement in plants: (2023 Board)
options: It is due to stimulus of touch and temperature.
It is a growth related movement.

It is observed only in roots and not in stems.
explanation: Tropic movements are growth-related, directional movements of plant parts in response to a stimulus (like light, gravity, water, or chemicals).

This is false — tropic movement specifically depends on the direction from which the stimulus is received; that is the defining feature of a tropism.

text: The resultant magnetic field at point 'P' situated midway between two parallel wires (placed horizontally) each carrying a steady current I in the same direction is (2023 Board)
options: in the same direction as the current in the wires.
explanation: For two parallel wires carrying current in the same direction, the magnetic fields produced at the midpoint between them are equal in magnitude but opposite in direction, so they cancel out to give a net field of zero.
whyWrong: The two fields act in opposite directions at the midpoint and cancel, rather than adding up along the current's direction.
The fields cancel out entirely rather than pointing downward.
The fields at the midpoint point in opposite directions and cancel, rather than combining to point upward.

text: Assertion (A): The colour of aqueous solution of copper sulphate turns colourless when a piece of lead is added to it. Reason (R): Lead is more reactive than copper, and hence displaces copper from its salt solution. (2023 Board)

text: Assertion (A): Genes inherited from the parents decide the sex of a child. Reason (R): X chromosome in a male child is inherited from his father. (2023 Board)
